title: First Response Field Guide and Quiet Window Stencils
author: Maya Chen
summary: A concise field guide for first responders that standardizes immediate triage actions, containment steps, short-form 'quiet window' customer message stencils, and a set of templates for status page and internal bridge communications. Designed to be usable from a pager notification within the first 10 minutes of an incident.
body:
Overview

This document is a compact, action-oriented handbook for the first 0–60 minutes of an incident. It balances fast decision-making with safe containment patterns and provides pre-approved communication stencils (internal and external) tailored to short, customer-facing "quiet windows" when we must limit updates to avoid noise while we stabilize. Use this guide for real incidents and as the canonical source for game-day scenarios focused on communication discipline and rapid stabilization.

Scope
- Audience: on-call engineers, bridge owners, SREs, incident managers, and CS escalation leads.
- Applies to: service outages, severe latency regressions, rolling errors / 5xx spikes, model-serving degradations (quality or performance), and multi-region network incidents.
- Not for: routine tickets, planned maintenance, or postmortem write-ups (see Postmortem Playbook for that process).

Key Roles and Rapid Ownership
1) Pagered responder (first responder): acknowledge within 5 minutes. Responsible for initial triage and reporting.
2) Bridge owner: sets up bridge, coordinates cross-team responders.
3) Incident commander (IC): takes charge when incident is escalated past containment.
4) Communications lead (Comms): curates internal and customer messages; owns status page updates.
5) Support liaison (CS): coordinates with Customer Success for high-touch customers.

Severity Classification (quick lookup)
- Sev 1: Global outage or >50% customers impacted / critical SLOs (P0). Immediate bridge and exec notification.
- Sev 2: Significant regional outage or critical feature down for a subset of customers (P1). Bridge within 15 minutes.
- Sev 3: Degraded performance or non-critical errors (P2). Monitor and triage; update next business-hour status if persistent.

(Quick table)
Impact | Time to ack | Bridge? | Customer notice
Sev 1 | <5m | Yes (immediate) | Yes (initial within 15m)
Sev 2 | <10m | Yes | Yes (within 30m)
Sev 3 | <30m | No unless escalated | Optional

Immediate Triage Decision Tree (0–10 minutes)
1) Acknowledge pager. Post to the on-call bridge channel: "ACK — assessing" with timestamp and short symptom.
2) Gather one-sentence observable: affected regions, error code or symptom (e.g., 502 spike), and percent of traffic impacted if available.
3) Run quick checks:
   - Is the control plane green? (kubectl/get pods Grafana / internal service health)
   - Are core infra metrics normal? (CPU, memory, network, disk I/O)
   - Is there a deployment / config change in the last 30 minutes? (deploy pipeline audit)
4) If root cause unknown and impact is Sev 1/2 -> bring bridge, escalate to Bridge Owner.

Immediate Action Checklist (up to first 30 minutes)
- Acknowledge and declare estimated severity.
- Capture and paste: pager payload, sample error logs (3 lines), Grafana dashboard permalink.
- Snapshot and pin: recent deploys, config rollouts, infra alerts.
- If noise suspected (e.g., noisy neighbor), use traffic controls: circuit-breaker, route-weight rollback, or throttling.
- If model inference latency high: remove model variants from routing pool (fallback to smaller model) per routing policy.
- When applicable, apply safe rollback or scale-up: do not re-deploy untested hotfixes without peer review.

Containment & Stabilization Play (recommended sequence)
1) Isolate the failing component: throttle traffic, disable feature flag, or move traffic to standby region.
2) Reproduce with a minimal query (if model-quality issue, use golden prompt set).
3) Engage adjacent owners: infra, runtime, model-onboarding, and networking.
4) Apply a conservative mitigation: scale-out, pin to older model, or enable degraded-mode route.
5) Verify KPIs: error rate back to baseline, P50/P95 latency, and CPU/KV cache saturation.

'Quiet Window' Customer Messaging: principles\- Keep messages brief and factual.\- Avoid speculation on root cause.\- Give expected cadence for next update.\- If impact is contained and we are stabilizing, use a short "quiet window" message to reduce inbound noise to CS and allow responders to focus.

Quiet Window Stencils (customer-facing)
- Initial short notice (for Sev 1/2):
  Subject: "[Service] Incident — degradation detected"
  Body: "We are aware of an issue affecting [feature/region]. Our team is investigating and has initiated mitigation steps. We will provide an update in 30 minutes or sooner.
  Customer impact: [brief summary e.g., elevated error rates for API endpoints in us-west-2].
  Next update: in 30 minutes.
  — Redwood Inference Status Team"
- Quiet window stabilization notice (if progress):
  Subject: "[Service] Stabilizing — update"
  Body: "We have applied a mitigation that is reducing customer impact. Traffic is being routed to a fallback model and error rates are trending down. We will continue to monitor and will follow up with a detailed update after verification.
  Estimated next update: 60 minutes.
  — Redwood Inference Status Team"
- If incident will require prolonged investigation (proactive):
  Subject: "[Service] Ongoing incident — next steps"
  Body: "We continue to investigate a disruption affecting [scope]. For customers who need immediate help, open a support ticket and tag 'incident-xxxx'. We will publish periodic updates on the status page: [status.redwood.ai/xxxxx]."

Status Page & Internal Bridge Templates (examples)
- Minimal status payload (JSON) for status page (fill placeholders before sending):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-YYYYMMDD-0001",
  "summary": "High error rate for /v1/generate in us-west-2",
  "impact": "Partial outage",
  "started_at": "2026-02-18T13:20:00Z",
  "status": "investigating",
  "next_update_minutes": "30"
}

- Internal bridge pinned summary (one-liner for Execs/Leads):
"INC-0001 — us-west-2 /v1/generate 502 spike affecting ~22% of requests. Mitigation: route to fallback model; errors dropping. IC: @name; Comms: @name."

Prescribed Escalation Triggers
- Escalate to IC: impact increases >25% in 10 minutes, or mitigation does not improve error rate by 50% in 30 minutes.
- Escalate to Execs: Sev 1 or when large customers (>= 5 enterprise customers) show major impact.
- Escalate to Legal/Security: if data exfiltration or unauthorized access suspected.

Post-Containment: evidence capture checklist (first actions before teardown)
- Preserve logs (export last 2 hours), Grafana snapshots, and query traces.
- Record all commands and rollbacks (shell history segment or Runbook audit).
- Take a TTL snapshot of model cache state if model inference issue.
- Ensure status page and CS tickets have consistent incident ID.

Short Postmortem Acceptance Criteria (IC sign-off)
- Timeline with timestamps for key events.
- Root cause hypothesis and why mitigation worked.
- Action items with owners and due dates.
- Customer impact statement.
- Close loop with patch or automated test if required.

Game-Day Syllabus (communication-focused)
- Objective: practice discipline for quiet-window messaging and rapid stabilization without over-communicating.
- Exercises (per quarter):
  1) 10-minute triage sprint: single engineer responds; must produce initial customer notice and Bridge summary.
  2) 30-minute stabilization: introduce a noisy neighbor; run traffic control actions and validate KPIs.
  3) Postmortem tabletop: simulate executive escalation and produce one-page incident brief.

On-Call Handoff & Handoff Checklist (end of shift)
- Current active incidents (IDs) and status.
- Any ongoing quiet windows and when next update is due.
- Open PRs or deployments that may affect service.
- Contact list for immediate escalation: IC, Comms, CS owner.
- A short note: "I left it at: {mitigation applied}, watch {metric} for 30m".

Operational tips and guardrails
- Do not hotpatch without peer review unless explicitly approved by IC.
- Avoid wide-scope rollbacks at night—prefer targeted route changes or throttles.
- Prefer temporary feature-flag disablement to code changes when possible.

References and Links
- Status page authoring guide: /confluence/product-docs/status-page-authoring
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026
- Model fallback routing policy: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/routing-policy

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: SRE Tech Ops (oncall-maintenance@redwood.ai).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev 1 incident.

Appendix: Copy-paste internal bridge message examples
- Initial: "ACK @channel — investigating elevated 502s for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Snapshot: https://grafana/permalink. Est. severity: P1."
- Stabilizing: "Mitigation applied (route to fallback model). Error rate down 60% in 12m. Monitoring for recurrence."

End of guide.

If you adopt or modify any of the stencils in this document, add your obsoleted versions to the doc history and notify the SRE Tech Ops owner.
